newsitem.title: UK: Brent paper perks up, wet North Sea in standoff.
newsitem.headline: Brent paper perks up, wet North Sea in standoff.

text.p: Paper Brent perked up early on Wednesday after the release of mildly supportive U.S. inventory data but wet North Sea markets were stuck in a standoff as sellers met resistance to higher offers.
IPE July Brent was eight cents firmer at $20.08 while the intermonth cash spread also edged further into backwardation, June/July valued at +4 cents after +2 traded late on Tuesday.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) said U.S. crude stocks fell by 5.9 million barrels last week as refiners ratcheted up gasoline production ahead of the traditional start of the driving season this weekend.
But while U.S. demand held up well, European buyers sat on their hands waiting to see whether a recent upturn in margins could be sustained.

Dated Brent was expected to hold the upper end of Tuesday's broad trading range between July -25 and -10 cents amid talk that a U.S. refiner would be picking up another early June cargo to fill a VLCC sailing trans-Atlantic.

Most other North Sea grades were offered firmer, as sellers eyed thin supply in the first half of June. Forties and Oseberg were particularly scarce but two Flotta cargoes were also cancelled on Wednesday.
Traders said Conoco's MacCulloch field, which was expected on stream at the end of this month, may now not start pumping crude into the Flotta system until early July.
Conoco officials were not immediately available for comment.
Brent Contracts for Difference were actively talked a shade firmer than late on Tuesday but no deals were reported.

The balance of this week and next week's dates (May 27-30) were worth July Brent -15/-10 cents, holding a five-cent backwardation over the following week. Two June 5-7 Brents were nominated loading dates and were passing through the paper chains, dealers said. --Mark Thompson, London +44 171 542 7930
